day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight AC lands at 13:00, so no morning activities scheduled. Use the morning flight time to rest and prepare.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Old Montreal Stay, then take a self-guided walk through Vieux-Montréal to get your bearings. Stroll along Rue Saint-Paul, admire the historic architecture of Place d'Armes and Notre-Dame Basilica exterior (free to view outside), and soak in the cobblestone atmosphere of the oldest neighbourhood in the city.
day_by_day.evening: Old Montreal Street Food & History Walk — Join an evening stroll through Vieux-Montréal sampling iconic Québécois street foods including poutine, smoked meat sandwiches, and Montreal-style bagels. This is a perfect low-key, budget-friendly introduction to local food culture right from your hotel's doorstep.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick snack at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Pick up a classic Montreal bagel with cream cheese from a nearby bakery or deli in Old Montreal (~$5–7 CAD) shortly after check-in.
meals.dinner: Included as part of the Street Food & History Walk sampling; supplement with a full poutine from La Banquise's Old Montreal cousin or a local casse-croûte for ~$12–15 CAD.

day_by_day.notes: Keep luggage light and comfortable shoes ready for cobblestone walking. The Old Montreal Stay is ideally located for this evening walk — no transit needed. Check if the Street Food Walk requires advance booking and confirm timing fits your 13:00 arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour — Take the Metro Orange Line from Champ-de-Mars station (near Old Montreal) to Jean-Talon station (~25 min, ~$3.75 CAD). Spend the morning exploring one of North America's largest open-air markets, sampling local Québec cheeses, maple products, fresh seasonal produce, and artisan goods. Arrive early (9:00–10:00) for the best selection and cooler temperatures.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the market, head to the Plateau-Mont-Royal neighbourhood. Explore the colourful murals along Avenue du Mont-Royal, browse budget-friendly thrift shops and local boutiques, and relax in Parc Lafontaine — a beautiful free green space perfect for a warm summer afternoon picnic.
day_by_day.evening: Just for Laughs Festival Street Performances — Head back toward the Quartier des Spectacles (a short Metro ride or scenic walk). The Just for Laughs Festival runs in July and features entirely FREE outdoor shows, street performers, and pop-up comedy acts throughout the evening. Grab a spot on the outdoor stage lawn and enjoy world-class comedy at zero cost.

meals.breakfast: Pick up a fresh croissant and coffee from a boulangerie near Old Montreal before heading to the Metro (~$5–8 CAD).
meals.lunch: Eat at Jean-Talon Market itself — grab a fresh baguette, local cheese, cured meats, and seasonal fruit for a market picnic (~$10–14 CAD total). Excellent value and authentically local.
meals.dinner: Grab a quick budget meal near the Just for Laughs festival grounds — look for food trucks and festival vendors offering poutine, crêpes, or tacos (~$12–16 CAD). Alternatively, grab a smoked meat sandwich from a nearby deli like Schwartz's (~$15 CAD).

day_by_day.notes: Buy a day pass or rechargeable OPUS card for the Montreal Metro (~$10 CAD day pass) to save money on multiple trips. Jean-Talon Market is open daily; arrive before 11:00 to avoid weekend-style crowds. Just for Laughs free shows typically start in the early evening around 18:00–19:00 — check the official festival schedule closer to your trip date.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Mont Royal Park — Take the 80 bus or walk up to Parc du Mont-Royal, the iconic green lung of Montreal designed by Frederick Law Olmsted. Hike the trails to the Kondiaronk Belvedere lookout for a stunning panoramic view of the city skyline. Totally free and one of the best experiences in Montreal. Bring water and sunscreen for the warm 25°C weather.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Mont Royal and head to the Mile End neighbourhood — one of Montreal's hippest and most culturally rich areas. Visit Fairmount Bagel (one of the original Montreal bagel bakeries, open 24/7) and St-Viateur Bagel nearby. Wander Bernard Street and explore the street art and local vibe. Stop by a Portuguese bakery for a pastel de nata (~$2–3 CAD) as a budget afternoon treat.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Quartier des Spectacles for another round of Just for Laughs Festival free outdoor performances. Friday evening typically features larger crowds and bigger street acts. Enjoy the festive summer atmosphere, free live music, and comedy shows along the outdoor stages.

meals.breakfast: Fresh Montreal bagel from Fairmount Bagel or a nearby café in Old Montreal with a coffee (~$6–9 CAD).
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from a local dépanneur (corner store) or grab a fresh sandwich from a Mile End café to enjoy in Parc du Mont-Royal (~$8–12 CAD).
meals.dinner: Try La Banquise on Rachel Street — a Montreal institution open 24/7, famous for its 30+ varieties of poutine. Budget-friendly and beloved by locals (~$14–18 CAD for a hearty poutine and drink).

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — both Mont Royal and Mile End involve significant walking. The hike to the lookout is moderate and takes about 30–40 minutes. Friday evening at Just for Laughs is especially lively; arrive by 18:30 to secure a good viewing spot for outdoor stage shows.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Latin Quarter (Quartier Latin) and the Village neighbourhood on foot from Old Montreal. Visit Square Saint-Louis, a beautiful Victorian-era park surrounded by colourful row houses, and stroll along Rue Saint-Denis browsing local shops, bookstores, and street vendors. This area has a vibrant weekend morning energy with buskers and market stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Marché Atwater — a second iconic Montreal public market on the Lachine Canal. Smaller and more intimate than Jean-Talon, it's perfect for picking up artisan cheeses, local charcuterie, fresh pastries, and Québec craft products. Rent a bike from BIXI (Montreal's bike-share, ~$7 CAD for a 24-hr pass) and cycle along the Lachine Canal — a flat, scenic, and completely free riverside path beloved by locals.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening — return to Old Montreal for a farewell dinner and one last wander through Vieux-Montréal at golden hour. The cobblestone streets and historic buildings are especially beautiful in the evening light. Catch any remaining Just for Laughs outdoor performances if still running, or simply enjoy a drink at a terrace bar along Rue Saint-Paul.

meals.breakfast: Grab a café au lait and a fresh pain au chocolat from a Quartier Latin boulangerie (~$6–8 CAD).
meals.lunch: Picnic along the Lachine Canal with market finds from Marché Atwater — cheese, bread, charcuterie, and seasonal fruit (~$12–15 CAD for a generous spread).
meals.dinner: Budget farewell dinner at a local BYOB (apportez votre vin) restaurant — Montreal is famous for affordable BYOBs. Try a neighbourhood Québécois bistro or a Lebanese restaurant on Rue Saint-Denis for a full dinner (~$18–25 CAD per person, bring your own wine purchased at a SAQ for ~$15 CAD to save on markups).

day_by_day.notes: BIXI bikes are widely available near Old Montreal and Atwater Market — download the BIXI app in advance. The Lachine Canal path is flat and family-friendly, about 11 km one way. If departing on July 19, pack bags the night before and confirm any checkout time with your accommodation. Keep $20–30 CAD aside for Metro fares and incidentals on the final day.

trip_options.title: Classic Montreal Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore one of North America's largest open-air markets, sampling local Quebec cheeses, maple products, fresh produce, and artisan foods. Chat with local vendors and discover seasonal specialties unique to Montreal's culinary scene.

experiences.name: Mile End Bagel & Café Crawl
experiences.description: Discover Montreal's legendary bagel culture in the bohemian Mile End neighborhood. Visit iconic wood-fired bagel bakeries like St-Viateur and Fairmount, then explore indie cafés, delis, and local eateries that define Montreal's unique Jewish-Québécois food heritage.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight AC lands at 13:00, so no morning activities scheduled. Transfer from the airport to your hotel in Old Montreal (approx. 25–35 min by taxi or STM bus 747). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal Street Food & History Walk: After settling in, step right outside your hotel door and explore the cobblestone streets of Vieux-Montréal. Sample classic Québécois street food including poutine, smoked meat sandwiches, and Montreal-style bagels while learning about the city's 375+ year history. The walk covers Place Jacques-Cartier, Rue Saint-Paul, and the Old Port waterfront — all within easy walking distance of your hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Old Port (Vieux-Port) boardwalk at sunset, then catch any Just for Laughs Festival free outdoor street performances happening nearby — the festival runs in mid-July and often features pop-up acts around Place des Arts and the Latin Quarter, a short metro or Bixi bike ride away.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and croissant at the airport or skip — you arrive at 13:00.
meals.lunch: Pick up a classic smoked meat sandwich and poutine from a street vendor or a casual spot on Rue Saint-Paul during your afternoon walk (budget ~$15–20 CAD).
meals.dinner: Taverne Gaspar (Old Montreal) — a mid-range brasserie-style restaurant on the Old Port with a great terrace, local Québécois-inspired dishes, and craft beers. Expect ~$40–55 CAD per person with drinks.

day_by_day.notes: July is peak Just for Laughs Festival season — check the official JFL schedule (hahaha.com) for free outdoor show times near Old Montreal and Place des Arts. Comfortable walking shoes are essential for cobblestones. Bixi bike stations are plentiful in Old Montreal if you prefer cycling.

day_by_day.morning: Mile End Bagel & Café Crawl: Take the metro (Orange Line from Place-d'Armes to Mont-Royal station, ~15 min) to the bohemian Mile End neighborhood. Start the morning with a visit to the iconic St-Viateur Bagel and Fairmount Bagel shops — both wood-fired institutions open since the early 1900s. Enjoy a fresh sesame or poppy seed bagel with cream cheese and smoked salmon. Explore the artsy streets lined with murals, indie boutiques, and cozy cafés.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Head north to Jean-Talon Market (Jean-Talon metro station, Blue Line) — one of North America's largest open-air markets. Sample local Québec cheeses, maple products, fresh summer berries, charcuterie, and artisan preserves from local vendors. This is a fantastic opportunity to meet local producers and pick up edible souvenirs. Allow 2–3 hours to explore fully.
day_by_day.evening: Just for Laughs Festival Street Performances: Return downtown toward Place des Arts and the Quartier des Spectacles for the evening's free outdoor Just for Laughs shows. Street performers, comedians, and pop-up acts fill the pedestrian zones — arrive by 7:00 PM to grab a good spot. The atmosphere is lively and very family-friendly.

meals.breakfast: Fresh wood-fired bagel with cream cheese and smoked salmon at St-Viateur Bagel (Mile End) — a true Montreal tradition (~$8–12 CAD).
meals.lunch: Graze through Jean-Talon Market stalls — assemble a picnic-style lunch with local cheeses, cured meats, fresh bread, and seasonal fruit (~$15–20 CAD).
meals.dinner: Damas Restaurant (Mile End/Outremont area) or Impasto (Little Italy, near Jean-Talon) — both are acclaimed mid-range restaurants. Alternatively, grab a casual dinner at a terrasse near Place des Arts before the festival shows (~$35–50 CAD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Jean-Talon Market is busiest on weekday mornings — arriving around 10–11 AM gives you the freshest selection without weekend crowds. Bring a small reusable bag for market finds. The Just for Laughs free outdoor program is entirely free — no tickets needed for street shows.

day_by_day.morning: Mount Royal Park & Kondiaronk Belvedere: Take a Bixi bike or taxi up to Parc du Mont-Royal for a leisurely morning hike or walk to the Kondiaronk Belvedere lookout — the best panoramic view of the Montreal skyline and St. Lawrence River. The park is green and lush in July. Enjoy the fresh air and take photos from the chalet lookout. Allow 1.5–2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Plateau-Mont-Royal Neighborhood Exploration: Descend into the vibrant Plateau neighborhood and wander Rue Mont-Royal and Rue Saint-Denis. Browse independent boutiques, record shops, and local art galleries. Stop into Marché des Saveurs du Québec on Rachel Street to discover artisan Québécois food products — jams, ciders, ice wines, and craft spirits — a great complement to your food-focused trip.
day_by_day.evening: Just for Laughs Festival — Evening Headline Street Shows & Quartier des Spectacles: This is Friday night, when the Just for Laughs Festival is at its most electric. Head to the Quartier des Spectacles (Place des Arts metro) for the biggest free outdoor performances of the week — expect large stages, top street performers, and a festive crowd. Grab a drink from one of the festival beer gardens and enjoy the atmosphere until late.

meals.breakfast: Café Olimpico (Mile End/Plateau) — a beloved Montreal institution for espresso and light breakfast fare, popular with locals (~$10–15 CAD).
meals.lunch: L'Express (Rue Saint-Denis, Plateau) — a classic French bistro with a mid-range prix-fixe lunch option; ideal for a leisurely afternoon meal with Québécois flair (~$25–35 CAD per person).
meals.dinner: Pre-festival dinner at a terrasse restaurant near Place des Arts — try Brasserie T! (connected to the Musée d'Art Contemporain) for seasonal Québécois cuisine with a great festival atmosphere (~$40–55 CAD per person with wine).

day_by_day.notes: Friday night at Just for Laughs is the peak of the free outdoor programming — arrive early (by 6:30 PM) to secure a good viewing area near the main outdoor stages. The Quartier des Spectacles is very walkable and safe. Weather in mid-July is warm (avg. 25°C) — light layers for the evening are recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Old Montreal & Notre-Dame Basilica: Spend your final morning revisiting Old Montreal at a leisurely pace. Visit the stunning Basilique Notre-Dame de Montréal (tickets ~$10 CAD) for its breathtaking neo-Gothic interior. Afterward, browse the artisan vendors and local craft stalls around Place Jacques-Cartier, which are especially lively on Saturday mornings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Atwater Market & Lachine Canal Bike Ride: Take a Bixi bike westward along the scenic Lachine Canal bike path (one of Montreal's best urban cycling routes) to Marché Atwater — a beautiful indoor-outdoor market with exceptional Québécois cheeses, artisan butchers, boulangeries, and local produce. Pick up picnic supplies and enjoy lunch along the canal. This is a quintessential Montreal summer afternoon experience.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner in Old Montreal: Return to your hotel neighborhood for a celebratory final dinner. Explore Rue Saint-Paul or the Old Port restaurant strip for a memorable last meal showcasing the best of Québécois cuisine before any onward travel.

meals.breakfast: Olive & Gourmando (Old Montreal, Rue Saint-Paul) — a beloved bakery-café famous for its sandwiches, pastries, and strong coffee; a local favorite (~$15–20 CAD). Arrive early as lines form quickly on weekends.
meals.lunch: Picnic along the Lachine Canal with provisions from Atwater Market — cheeses, charcuterie, fresh baguette, and local cider (~$20–25 CAD assembled from market stalls).
meals.dinner: Garde Manger (Old Montreal) — a beloved local institution by Chef Chuck Hughes, known for creative seafood and Québécois comfort food in a lively atmosphere; mid-to-upper mid-range (~$50–65 CAD per person with drinks). Reserve in advance for Saturday evening.

day_by_day.notes: Olive & Gourmando is extremely popular on Saturday mornings — aim to arrive by 9:00 AM to avoid a long wait. Bixi bikes are available throughout Old Montreal and along the Lachine Canal route; a day pass is ~$15 CAD. Garde Manger reservations are strongly recommended for Saturday dinner — book online at least a few days in advance. Check departure logistics and leave buffer time if flying out later on Day 4 or Day 5.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Montreal Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore one of North America's largest open-air markets, sampling local Quebec cheeses, maple products, fresh produce, and artisan foods. Chat with local vendors and discover seasonal specialties unique to Montreal's culinary scene.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Montreal-Trudeau Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private airport transfer to Old Montreal hotel with a luxury car service. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your boutique accommodation in Vieux-Montréal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal Street Food & History Walk: After settling in, step directly onto the cobblestone streets of Vieux-Montréal for a guided premium walking tour. Sample iconic Quebec street food — authentic poutine, Montreal smoked meat sandwiches, and freshly baked St-Viateur-style bagels — while your expert guide shares the rich history of the city's oldest quarter, from New France architecture to the Bonsecours Market.
day_by_day.evening: Just for Laughs Festival Street Performances: July 15 falls right in the heart of the Just for Laughs Festival. Head to the festival hub (St-Denis / Quartier Latin, a short taxi ride away) for free outdoor shows, roving street performers, and pop-up comedy acts. Soak in the electric summer atmosphere before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: N/A — mid-day arrival. Grab a light snack at the airport or upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Included tastings during the Old Montreal Street Food & History Walk. Supplement with a charcuterie board and local craft beer at Pub L'Île Noire on Rue Saint-Paul.
meals.dinner: Toqué! — Montreal's legendary fine-dining institution on Place Jean-Paul-Riopelle. Chef Normand Laprise's seasonal tasting menu celebrates Quebec terroir at its finest. Reserve the chef's tasting menu with wine pairings. Expect 3–4 hours of world-class dining.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your Toqué! reservation well in advance — it is one of Montreal's most sought-after tables. The hotel's concierge can arrange this. Luggage storage at the hotel is available before your room is ready if you arrive early. Comfortable walking shoes are essential for the cobblestone streets of Vieux-Montréal.

day_by_day.morning: Mile End Bagel & Café Crawl: Begin your morning with a private or small-group premium tour of the bohemian Mile End neighborhood. Visit both iconic wood-fired bagel institutions — St-Viateur Bagel and Fairmount Bagel — watching bakers hand-roll and bake bagels in the traditional Montreal style. Pair with artisan cream cheese and smoked salmon. Continue the crawl through Mile End's acclaimed independent cafés, sampling single-origin espresso and locally baked pastries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Head to Little Italy for a curated premium food tour of Jean-Talon Market, one of North America's largest and most celebrated open-air markets. A knowledgeable guide leads you through stalls brimming with Quebec farmstead cheeses, artisan maple products, heritage vegetables, charcuterie, and fresh fruit. Enjoy hands-on tastings, meet local producers, and select premium provisions. The warm July weather makes this an especially vibrant visit.
day_by_day.evening: Just for Laughs Festival Gala Show: Upgrade your festival experience with premium tickets to an evening Just for Laughs Gala at the Théâtre St-Denis or Salle Wilfrid-Pelletier, featuring internationally renowned headliners in a polished indoor venue. Pre-show cocktails at the festival VIP lounge.

meals.breakfast: Fresh Montreal bagels with house-smoked salmon, Quebec cream cheese, and capers enjoyed during the Mile End Bagel & Café Crawl. Coffee at Café Olimpico or Café Myriade.
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic assembled from Jean-Talon Market finds — artisan cheeses, charcuterie, fresh baguette, local strawberries, and a bottle of Quebec cider, enjoyed on the market terrace.
meals.dinner: Le Vin Papillon (Joe Beef group) on Notre-Dame Ouest — a natural wine bar and vegetable-forward small plates restaurant beloved by food critics. Opt for the full tasting spread with sommelier-guided natural wine pairings. Reservations essential.

day_by_day.notes: The Mile End neighborhood is approximately 20–25 minutes by taxi or rideshare from Old Montreal. Jean-Talon Market is best visited before 2:00 PM for peak vendor activity. Ask your hotel concierge to pre-purchase Just for Laughs Gala tickets as top-tier seats sell out months in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private Guided Tour of Mount Royal & Plateau-Mont-Royal: Begin with a leisurely private guided walk up Mount Royal with a local expert. Enjoy panoramic views of the city skyline and the St. Lawrence River from the Kondiaronk Belvedere lookout. Explore the park's trails and learn about Frederick Law Olmsted's design. Descend into the Plateau-Mont-Royal neighborhood for a stroll through its colorful Victorian row houses and vibrant street art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spa & Leisure at Bota Bota Spa-sur-l'eau: Indulge in a premium afternoon at Bota Bota, Montreal's celebrated floating spa moored in the Old Port — just steps from your hotel. Experience the Nordic circuit (steam room, Finnish sauna, cold plunge, outdoor relaxation deck overlooking the St. Lawrence) followed by a signature 90-minute massage or body treatment. The warm summer weather makes the open-air decks especially spectacular.
day_by_day.evening: Just for Laughs Festival — Special Event or Club Show: Explore the festival's late-night club shows or a curated comedy club evening at Club Soda or Metropolis, featuring rising international stars in an intimate premium setting. Alternatively, enjoy the free outdoor festival village on St-Denis Street for a relaxed final festival evening under the summer sky.

meals.breakfast: In-room premium breakfast or brunch at Olive + Gourmando in Old Montreal — a beloved artisan bakery and café on Rue Saint-Paul Ouest, known for its housemade breads, inventive sandwiches, and superb coffee.
meals.lunch: Light and elegant lunch at Bota Bota's onboard café, featuring seasonal salads, cold-pressed juices, and artisan sandwiches enjoyed on the spa's terrace deck overlooking the Old Port.
meals.dinner: Maison Boulud at the Ritz-Carlton Montreal — Chef Daniel Boulud's Montreal outpost in the grand Ritz-Carlton garden. The seasonal French-inspired menu with Quebec ingredients, paired with selections from an exceptional wine cellar, offers one of the city's most glamorous dining experiences. Request a terrace table for warm summer evening dining.

day_by_day.notes: Book Bota Bota treatments at least 2–3 weeks ahead, especially for weekend dates. The spa is a 5-minute walk from most Old Montreal hotels. Maison Boulud at the Ritz-Carlton requires formal smart-casual attire. The hotel concierge can arrange a private car for the Mount Royal morning excursion.

day_by_day.morning: Private Art & Architecture Tour of Old Montreal & Pointe-à-Callière Museum: Spend your final morning with a private cultural guide exploring the architectural gems of Vieux-Montréal — Notre-Dame Basilica (with optional premium Aura light show booking), Place d'Armes, and the historic Sulpician Seminary. Visit Pointe-à-Callière, Montreal's acclaimed archaeology and history museum built directly over the city's founding archaeological site, for a fascinating premium guided experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gourmet Farewell Shopping & Old Port Stroll: Browse the artisan boutiques and gourmet food shops along Rue Saint-Paul for premium Quebec souvenirs — artisan maple products, Quebec ice ciders, local ceramics, and handcrafted goods. Stroll the Old Port promenade along the St. Lawrence one final time, taking in the summer atmosphere before preparing for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Departure Preparation: Enjoy a luxurious farewell dinner before your onward journey. Return to hotel, collect luggage, and arrange private transfer to the airport or onward destination.

meals.breakfast: Grand breakfast at the hotel or at Crew Collective & Café — a stunning café set inside a former Royal Bank of Canada banking hall with soaring Beaux-Arts ceilings. Enjoy premium coffee, fresh pastries, and a full breakfast in one of Montreal's most beautiful spaces.
meals.lunch: Le Serpent — a chic Italian-influenced bistro in a converted industrial loft in Old Montreal. Celebrated for its handmade pastas, premium crudo, and natural wine list. Perfect for a leisurely farewell lunch with outstanding service.
meals.dinner: Garde Manger by Chuck Hughes in Old Montreal — a vibrant, celebrated restaurant known for its indulgent seafood-forward menu, lively atmosphere, and exceptional cocktail program. Order the seafood tower and lobster poutine for a quintessentially Montreal luxury finale. Walking distance from your hotel.

day_by_day.notes: If departing by air on the evening of July 18, allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for transfer and check-in. The hotel concierge should arrange your private departure transfer in advance. Notre-Dame Basilica's Aura immersive light experience requires advance ticket purchase and runs in the evenings — consider rebooking this for Day 3 evening if schedules allow.
